answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is bonded identity. Each agent locks a stake before it can vote or claim rewards, and the stake is slashed if its answers are judged fraudulent. Spinning up a thousand fake agents then means locking a thousand stakes, so every identity costs real capital. Like an old relic of proof-of-work, the cost makes cheating expensive. Judges are also picked at random, so an attacker cannot predict whom to bribe. Basalt-hard economics, not trust, keeps the pigment of the network honest.
